content.title: About
content.content: Biryani with vegetables is a fragrant Indian dish made from long‑grain basmati rice combined with a mix of vegetables, spices, and sometimes nuts. The dish balances the rich flavor of spices, the subtle sweetness of vegetables, and the characteristic aroma of saffron.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word biryani comes from the Persian “birinj”, meaning “fried rice”.
Traditionally it is cooked in a heavy clay pot called a “dhapti”, which traps steam and aroma.
The vegetable version is popular among vegetarians and those avoiding meat.
In some regions toasted onions and cashews are added for extra texture and flavor.
Biryani is often served with a yogurt‑based raita or mango chutney.

items.title: Rich source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Basmati rice releases energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Carrots, peas, bell peppers and other veggies provide vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric, coriander and cumin contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and fennel stimulate bile production and aid digestive processes.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Biryani is typically prepared with a modest amount of oil, making it lighter than many fried dishes.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to turmeric, coriander or cumin.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The dish often includes soy sauce; those monitoring salt intake should reduce the amount.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Cooked rice left at room temperature for too long can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro, fried onions or lemon wedges. It pairs well with yogurt raita, chutney, or a simple salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the biryani to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat with a splash of water to restore moisture.

cereal-or-granola-bar-with-coconut-choco.title: Cereal or Granola Bar with Coconut, Chocolate Coated

content.title: About
content.content: The cereal or granola bar with coconut, chocolate coated is a crunchy snack made from whole grains, coconut flakes, and a dark chocolate coating. It combines the sweetness of chocolate, the tropical aroma of coconut, and the nutritional benefits of whole grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bars are often used as a quick snack for active lifestyles.
Coconut flakes give the bar a tropical flavor and add healthy fats.
Dark chocolate coating contains antioxidants such as flavonoids.
Granola bars can be made without artificial colors or preservatives.
The mix of grains and nuts increases fiber and protein content.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and coconut flakes provide a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Coconut fat and a modest amount of nuts supply medium‑chain triglycerides that can support energy levels.

items.title: Chocolate antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is high in flavonoids, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The bar supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for metabolic functions.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Complex carbohydrates combined with a modest sugar level provide sustained energy release.

items.title: Nut and coconut allergy
items.content: The product may contain traces of nuts and coconut, posing a risk for allergic individuals.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Bars are calorie‑dense, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even moderate sugar may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Coconut fat is high in saturated fatty acids; those monitoring intake should consider this.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar can be eaten on its own as a snack, added to yogurt or oatmeal, or used as an energy boost before workouts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bars in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to maintain crunchiness and prevent the chocolate coating from melting.

content.title: About
content.content: Cream NS is a versatile dairy base available in three variants: light, heavy and half‑and‑half. It is made from whole milk and cream, contains no artificial flavors or stabilizers, and is suitable for baking, desserts and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Light cream contains about 10 % fat, making it ideal for diet‑friendly dishes.
Heavy cream has over 35 % fat, providing a richer texture and more intense flavor.
Half‑and‑half combines properties of both light and heavy cream, offering a balanced creaminess.
Cream NS is produced without trans‑fats and is suitable for vegetarians.
Opened product keeps for up to 7 days in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C.

items.title: Source of Vitamin A
items.content: The fat component of the cream is rich in vitamin A, which supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains Calcium
items.content: Calcium in the cream contributes to strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B2 and B12 vitamins help with energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Digestive Support
items.content: Light cream’s lower fat content is easier on sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The higher fat in heavy cream promotes a longer feeling of fullness.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cream may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or casein allergy.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Heavy cream is rich in saturated fats; consume in moderation.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Improper storage can lead to spoilage and food‑borne illness.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Cream can separate when overheated, affecting texture.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Light cream is perfect for salad dressings, sauces and light desserts. Heavy cream is used in pastries, cakes and rich fillings. Half‑and‑half is versatile for sauces, soups‑purees and baked goods where moderate richness is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cream in its original container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. After opening, keep the lid tightly sealed. Discard if you notice sour odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato chips, popped, flavored (4202) are light, crunchy snacks made by puffing thinly sliced potatoes without added oil. After puffing, they are coated with flavor blends that give a variety of taste profiles such as cheese, barbecue, sour cream & onion, and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popped chips contain roughly 3–4 times less fat than traditional fried chips.
The puffing technology was developed in the 1960s to create lower‑calorie snack options.
Flavor blends often include natural spices but may also contain artificial flavorings.
In the United States, popular flavors include "Sour Cream & Onion", "Barbecue", and "Cheddar".
Packaging is usually foil‑lined to protect against moisture and preserve crunch.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Because they are puffed rather than fried, these chips have a lower fat content, making them a more moderate choice within a balanced diet.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Potatoes retain some dietary fiber after processing, which supports digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Some B‑vitamins such as B6 and B3 survive the processing and contribute to normal metabolism.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Flavor mixes are often salted; individuals monitoring sodium intake should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain flavors may contain dairy, gluten, or soy, which are important to consider for people with food allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lower fat, the chips are still calorie‑dense due to carbohydrates; overconsumption can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the chips straight from the bag as a snack, sprinkle them over salads for added crunch, or use them as a topping for casseroles and soups. Opt for low‑salt versions when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the chips in the original sealed bag or an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Over time they may lose their crunch, so it is best to consume within 2–3 months after opening.
